answer: Domain registration age with registrar history is the check: a domain held and renewed with one registrar for a decade. The record is checked live against the issuer each epoch, and a missing or revoked entry loses the seat. A farm faking 481 aliases needs 481 separate aged domains, each built over years, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. A juniper marker runs through the scheme: every claim is checkable, every fake pays separately, and the basalt ledger turns 481 aliases into 481 bills while the grove path for the honest stays a single payment.
